# Jane Andrews

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c23 P41](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0041)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea  <sub>[v3 c8 P18](../source/v03-c08.md#nw-v03-c08-p0018), [v3 c18 P3](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0003)</sub>
- **Role:** school teacher  <sub>[v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v3 c18 P3](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0003)</sub>

## Appearance

Jane is described as plain, neat, and prim. At her lavish wedding, she wore an abundance of white satin, tulle, lace, roses, orange blossoms, and diamonds, which almost obscured her small figure from sight.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004), [v3 c41 P9](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0009)_

## Personality

Jane is sensible, practical, composed, and conscientious. She is steady and unflappable, possessing steady nerves that do not rattle under pressure during examinations. Unpoetical by nature, she approaches work with a straightforward, plodding manner. Although ladylike and well-behaved, she believes a teacher must be a little cross to maintain order in the classroom.

_Sources: [v1 c31 P30](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0030), [v1 c32 P18](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0018), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v2 c4 P2](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0002), [v2 c13 P65](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0065), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059)_

## History

Jane grew up in Avonlea, attending the local school and participating in a childhood Story Club with her friends Anne, Diana, and Ruby. During a school picnic, she was saved from drowning in the Lake of Shining Waters by her father when she leaned out too far. She later joined the Queen's Academy preparation class, passed the Entrance examinations with steady composure, and pursued Second Class teacher's certification, taking top honors in the domestic science course. Upon graduating, she secured a position teaching school at Newbridge, where her work earned her a place on the Inspector's Roll of Honor. Active in community life, Jane served as the chairman of the re-shingling and painting committee for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. After teaching at Newbridge, she accepted a teaching post in Avonlea before moving to teach on the western prairies. Prior to her departure for the West, she carried out a proposal of marriage to Anne on behalf of her shy brother Billy, which Anne declined. After returning home from the West, Jane married Mr. Inglis, a Winnipeg millionaire, in a splendid ceremony and went on a wedding tour to Europe.

_Sources: [v1 c14 P68](../source/v01-c14.md#nw-v01-c14-p0068), [v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v1 c32 P18](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0018), [v1 c34 P11](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0011), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v2 c4 P2](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0002), [v2 c6 P10](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0010), [v2 c28 P3](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0003), [v3 c8 P12](../source/v03-c08.md#nw-v03-c08-p0012), [v3 c11 P0](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0000), [v3 c18 P3](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0003), [v3 c35 P44](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0044), [v3 c39 P18](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0018), [v3 c39 P27](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0027), [v3 c39 P35](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0035), [v3 c41 P9](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0009)_

## Quotes

> I guess we’ll get on all right. The main thing will be to keep order and a teacher has to be a little cross to do that. If my pupils won’t do as I tell them I shall punish them.  <sub>[v2 c4 P2](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0002)</sub>

> I’d wish to be rich and beautiful and clever.  <sub>[v2 c13 P32](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0032)</sub>

> A poem is lines and verses.  <sub>[v2 c13 P65](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0065)</sub>

> Billy wants to marry you. He’s always been crazy about you—and now father has given him the upper farm in his own name and there’s nothing to prevent him from getting married. But he’s so shy he couldn’t ask you himself if you’d have him, so he got me to do it. I’d rather not have, but he gave me no peace till I said I would, if I got a good chance. What do you think about it, Anne?  <sub>[v3 c8 P12](../source/v03-c08.md#nw-v03-c08-p0012)</sub>
